- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/late horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) or negative, model often underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially for first 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent days.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast slope in 3–5 day window.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 10-day average, adjust toward mean.
- High sentiment + high forecast = overconfidence; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high if sentiment >0.8.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative values, model underestimates; add 0.1–0.3 to early forecast values.
- Forecast errors are more severe in 20–30 day horizon; apply exponential decay weighting to later days if sentiment is volatile.
